decode
·
Stopped

at

ﬁrst

PIVOT after though: the answer is the
library
annexe. Fix: after any concrete detail, keep listening for one more
clause.
Calibration
script
Tutor: Good morning. Today we practise hearing speakers change their minds. I will read a short exchange, and
you tell me what was ﬁnally decided.
Student A: Shall we meet on Tuesday to plan this?
Tutor: Tuesday works. Actually, no, I teach all afternoon. Make it Wednesday morning, ten o'clock.
Student A: Wednesday at ten. Fine.
Key: Tutor (opening the lesson, then ﬁxing a meeting) and Student A; the purpose is to show a speaker
reversing a ﬁrst answer; the ﬁnal time is Wednesday at ten, the pivot is 'Actually, no'.
Cycle
1
scripts
1. I will interview people at the market on Friday, but the stalls shut early that day, so Thursday it is.
Key: Thursday. Pivot word: but. · Trap: PIVOT
2. The questionnaire has twenty-ﬁve questions. However, our pilot showed people stop at ﬁfteen, so we are
keeping ﬁfteen. [stress on ﬁfteen]
Key: Fifteen. Pivot word: however. · Trap: BAIT
3. Student A: The bus stop is two hundred metres from the library.
Student B: Actually, it is nearer three hundred. I paced it yesterday.
Key: About three hundred metres; Student B corrected it. Pivot word: actually. · Trap: PIVOT
4. We will hand out the forms at eight, I mean eight thirty, once the gates are unlocked.
Key: Eight thirty. Pivot phrase: I mean. · Trap: PIVOT

Cycle
2
scripts
5. Put the tally sheets in the blue folder. On second thought, make it the green one. The blue ones belong to the
other group.
Key: The green folder. Pivot phrase: on second thought. · Trap: PIVOT
6. Originally we wanted to sample two hundred households. Now, with only one weekend, it is a hundred and
twenty.
Key: A hundred and twenty. Signal word: originally. · Trap: BAIT
7. We could post the forms to residents. Alternatively, we stand at the station exit and ask commuters face to
face, which is quicker, and that is what we will do.
Key: Ask commuters face to face at the station exit. Pivot word: alternatively. · Trap: PIVOT
8. The results are due on the ninth. No wait, that is the presentation. The results are due on the sixth.
Key: The sixth. Pivot phrase: no wait. Own sentence, e.g. 'The meeting is on Monday. Actually, it is on Tuesday.'
· Trap: PIVOT
9. I would say we cut each interview to ten minutes. Having said that, our pilot ran ﬁfteen and nobody
complained, so ﬁfteen it is.
Key: Fifteen minutes. Pivot phrase: having said that. Own sentence, e.g. 'We could ask forty people. Having
said that, time is short, so thirty.' · Trap: PIVOT
10. The report should be ﬁve pages. That said, the department allows eight if there are charts, so aim for eight.
Key: Eight pages. Pivot phrase: that said. Own sentence, e.g. 'I would start at nine. That said, ten is ﬁne if the
bus is late.' · Trap: PIVOT

Case
ﬁle
·
Planning
the
Garden
Visitor
Study
Tutor: Right, you two have picked the public garden for your ﬁeld study. Let's settle the design today. What is
your research question?
Student A: I thought we would count how many people come in each day. [brisk]
Tutor: That is easy to do, but a head count only tells you how many, not what they do there. What about how
long people stay?
Student B: I'd wondered about asking which ﬂowers they like best. [pause] Though I suppose that is a diﬀerent
study.
Tutor: It is. Keep to the length of the visit.
Student A: Fine. Then observation. Fifteen-minute blocks, three times a day?
Tutor: Hmm, ﬁfteen minutes is too short to see anyone arrive and leave. Actually, make the blocks thirty
minutes. A full hour would wear you out.
Student B: And which day? Saturday, I would say, because that is when most people visit.
Student A: Okay, but there is a ﬂower market in the car park every Saturday, and it would distort the numbers.
[stress on Saturday] Sunday is much calmer.
Tutor: Then Sunday each week. Now, how will you record the timings?
Student B: I was going to suggest a tablet, but we only have one between us, and the battery lasts about an
hour. So, paper forms on a clipboard.
Student A: We could use a voice recorder instead and talk quietly into it.
Tutor: People would hear you and feel watched. [shaking head] Stay with paper. Now the sample. How many
visitors will you time?
Student A: Two hundred, ideally. [conﬁdent]
Tutor: [doubtful] Two hundred is ambitious for two people. Originally the department asked for a hundred per
team, but that was before they cut the study to one weekend, so sixty will do. You also plan a few short
interviews. How long should each one last?
Student B: Five minutes each? [hopeful]
Tutor: Five sounds reasonable. No wait, people will not stand around that long. Three minutes at most. Finally,
when can you send me the plan?
Student B: Monday? [uncertain]
Student A: Friday would be safer. We need the weekend to rewrite.
Tutor: Friday would suit me, but the ethics panel meets on Thursday and has to read the plan ﬁrst. So
Wednesday at the latest.
Student A: Right. Wednesday. [ﬂat]
